status: Stereo/reference audit only; no isolated instrument ground truth

referenceWindows.purpose: Relatively brighter, coherent central attack/harmonic material
referenceWindows.preferredSpatialObservation: Mid can emphasize this material; do not confuse Mid with an instrument identity.
referenceWindows.contamination: Bass, chords, earlier tails and lower/wide components coexist. The window is only .2 s, not a clean full-timbre query.

referenceWindows.preferredSpatialObservation: Side strongly retains this band, unlike direct L/R averaging.
referenceWindows.contamination: This band can be the third harmonic of a lower note, not necessarily a F5 fundamental. The full Side signal also includes reverberation and other stereo sources.

unsafeReferences.reason: A newly increasing 466/1398 family coexists with 698/2095 material. Not an isolated second instrument, despite the useful change in spectral balance.
Multiple overlapping attacks/tails and changing stereo phase. Do not concatenate the dominant peaks into one voice or treat the whole window as a pure second reference.

conclusions: Different bands have strongly different stereo structure in the original mixture as well as 07, so this is not solely a Demucs artifact.
A direct arithmetic L/R average suppresses substantial Side energy and can bias both pitch analysis and reference embeddings toward the brighter central partials.
Neither a solo exposure nor a stationary independent pan position for exactly two instruments has been established.
Stereo chorus, detuning, all-pass effects, reverberation, layered patches and different instruments can all explain frequency-dependent stereo shape.
The two proposed reference observations are contrasts, not two verified complete timbres. Keep an unassigned residual layer.
